Next week is the busiest week of the season, so let me tell you how it is going to work. On Monday, I'm meeting the six singers who are still in the competition. Each of them is getting forty minutes with me, one by one. On Tuesday and Wednesday, we are rehearsing with the band, and on Thursday the camera team is coming in for a full run-through. Friday is tentative. If everything is on track, we are going to give the singers the day off, because tired voices make mistakes. If not, we will use Friday to fix what is still not working. One singer has a sore throat right now, so I am going to keep her rehearsals short. I don't know yet who will win on Saturday. But I know one thing: they will all be ready.

In September, I'm starting an online course in music production. I have a full-time job in television, so I have to be realistic. I'm not going to study every night. That plan never works. Instead, I'm going to study three mornings a week, before work, from six to eight. My first assignment is due on the twentieth, and I have already penciled in a session with a friend who plays the drums. We are recording on a Sunday, because that is the only day when the studio is free. Will it be easy? Probably not. I think I will fall behind in the first month, because everybody does. But I have a calendar, I have a plan, and I have a reason. And when it gets hard, I'll remember why I started.

The producers set the date of the first live show. The team penciled in a studio slot for February. In the middle of February, the slot clashed with another recording. The music director said, 'I'll call the studio myself.' Two hours later, the new dates were firmed up. Now the team is on track for the first live show.
